item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-8101011b7f2a4897","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Ahead of Bangladesh’s January 2024 general election, Amnesty International reported systematic attacks on critical institutions, opposition leaders, independent media, and civil society, and said the 2023 Cyber Security Act retained draconian features of the Digital Security Act and could target critics, activists, and peaceful dissent.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 pre-election period and the government led by Sheikh Hasina.","ruler_attribution":"Amnesty attributes the legislation and authorities’ conduct to the Government of Bangladesh; Sheikh Hasina was prime minister during the period.","limitations":["This is an advocacy organization’s assessment and does not independently establish Hasina’s personal direction of each action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8101011b7f2a4897","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported that enforced disappearances and extrajudicial executions persisted, describing a pattern involving the Rapid Action Battalion and stating that the government had not adequately investigated or brought suspected perpetrators to justice despite prior commitments.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.10","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source evaluates the preceding five years and raises the issue in the 2023 UPR context; it is relevant to the 2023 governing period but is not limited to events occurring only in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment concerns Bangladesh’s government and law-enforcement agencies under Sheikh Hasina’s premiership.","limitations":["The passage summarizes a multi-year pattern and does not provide a complete 2023 incident inventory."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8101011b7f2a4897","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported continued suppression of peaceful protests through tear gas, rubber bullets, batons, stun grenades, water cannon, and sometimes lethal force, and called for impartial investigations, discipline of responsible officials, and release of arbitrarily detained protesters.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.6","2B.9","3B.2","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the authorities’ conduct in the period immediately preceding the November 2023 UPR.","ruler_attribution":"Amnesty attributes the conduct and requested remedies to Bangladeshi authorities under Sheikh Hasina’s government.","limitations":["The source does not identify individual orders by Hasina or quantify all incidents occurring specifically in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8101011b7f2a4897","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported that the death penalty continued to be imposed, including for some non-fatal offenses, and that the International Crimes Tribunal continued imposing death sentences in absentia amid due-process concerns.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.10","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source reports executions and death sentences from 2018–2022 and describes the continuing situation in the 2023 UPR period.","ruler_attribution":"The practices concern Bangladesh’s government and tribunal system during Sheikh Hasina’s tenure.","limitations":["The cited statistics largely predate 2023; the passage does not establish Hasina’s personal role in individual cases."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8101011b7f2a4897","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported at least five large-scale orchestrated attacks against Hindu minorities since 2019, persistent militarization of the Chittagong Hill Tracts despite the peace accord, and worsening insecurity and funding shortfalls affecting Rohingya refugees.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source describes conditions extending into the 2023 UPR period, while some examples date from 2019 onward.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes responsibility for state policies and protection failures to the Bangladeshi government under Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["The source does not quantify 2023 outcomes or distinguish central-government decisions from local or non-state actors in every incident."]},{"source_id":"SRC-af19bc1ce5ccc20f","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Reporters Without Borders reported a surge in pressure on Bangladeshi journalists, including judicial harassment, police violence, online harassment, attacks while reporting, and intimidation of families, while describing government initiatives to protect journalists as rare.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published 5 September 2023 and directly concerns the preceding weeks under Sheikh Hasina’s government.","ruler_attribution":"RSF addresses Sheikh Hasina’s government and attributes the broader protective failure to the authorities; it does not prove her personal involvement in each incident.","limitations":["RSF is an external press-freedom monitor and the report does not establish a complete chain of command for each abuse."]},{"source_id":"SRC-af19bc1ce5ccc20f","start_unit":12,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"RSF reported that Hasina’s cabinet approved a proposed Cyber Security Act on 7 August 2023 to replace the Digital Security Act; it described the bill as leaving broad room for arbitrary interpretation, being drafted without meaningful media consultation, and advancing before the January 2024 election while existing DSA cases would continue under the new law.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns a dated cabinet decision and legislative process in August–September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The cabinet and government were led by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina; the source does not establish that she personally drafted the bill.","limitations":["At publication, the bill still awaited parliamentary approval; the report records RSF’s assessment rather than a judicial finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-af19bc1ce5ccc20f","start_unit":13,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"RSF reported examples of online threats and a death fatwa against journalist Asad Noor, investigation of journalist Adhora Yasmean under the Digital Security Act, arrest warrants against journalists reporting on alleged official-linked wrongdoing, threats against families of exiled journalists, and physical attacks or expulsion of journalists while reporting in August 2023.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.3","3B.7","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The incidents and official responses described occurred in or immediately before August–September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes state-linked harassment, DSA investigations, and official silence or inaction to authorities under Sheikh Hasina; some attacks were by non-state or local actors.","limitations":["The source reports selected cases and does not demonstrate that Hasina personally ordered the conduct."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-b9011d4be8e77c59"],"batch_limitations":["The WFP page is largely a current country profile focused on 2024–2026 conditions and programs, not evidence specific to Sheikh Hasina during 2023; its general descriptions therefore do not provide a material period-fit fact for 2023–2023."]}
